guide-13.label: Restaurants by dish
guide-13.title: Where to eat in Gunsan by dish: jjamppong, kkotgejang (marinated blue crab), bakdae, agwijjim (braised monkfish), raw fish, tteokgalbi, kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) and bakeries
guide-13.summary: In Gunsan, you can eat jjamppong at the 9 restaurants on the Jjamppong Street on Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong, or at Ssangyong Banjeom, Bokseongnu and Jirinseong. For kkotgejang (marinated blue crab), go to Hanjuok, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch or Gyegok Garden. For bakdae, go to Saemangeum Hoetjip, Arirang or Namdo Bapsang, and for bread, go to Iseongdang or Yeongguk Ppangjip. Of the 172 Gunsan restaurants on this site, 20 have jjamppong dishes on the menu, 12 have gejang (marinated crab) such as kkotgejang, and 9 have agwi or agu (monkfish). Tteokgalbi and kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) are on 6 menus each, and kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) on 4. Places are grouped by dish. Gunsan City designations are noted (2026 Gunsan Matjip and Model Restaurant; 19 places on this page). We also note the 'Hundred-Year Shop' label in Korea Tourism Organization data (Ssangyong Banjeom, Unjeong Sikdang and Yurak Sikdang), features in broadcaster channel videos (6 places, including Iseongdang and Mannam Snack), Monday opening and parking. Where two sources give different values, both are listed.

body.heading: Gunsan restaurants by dish: of the 172 on this site, jjamppong is at 20, gejang (marinated crab) at 12, agwi or agu (monkfish) at 9, and tteokgalbi and kalguksu at 6 each
body.text: We grouped the signature and other menu items of the 172 Gunsan restaurants on this site by dish name. Jjamppong dishes are at 20 places (including jjamppong ramen; jjamppong bread is in the bread group). Gejang (marinated crab) such as kkotgejang (marinated blue crab), ganjang gejang (soy-marinated crab) and yangnyeom gejang (seasoned marinated crab) is at 12. Agwi or agu (monkfish) is at 9, tteokgalbi at 6, kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) at 6, kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) at 4, soba at 4 and bakdae at 3. At 11 places, the signature menu includes raw fish (saengseonhoe or hwareohoe), a raw fish set meal, sashimi or sushi. At 7, bread or hotteok is the signature item. For each group, we picked a few places and give the reason for each. We picked them by Gunsan City designation as a 2026 Gunsan Matjip or Model Restaurant, the 'Hundred-Year Shop' label in Korea Tourism Organization data, appearance in broadcaster channel videos, listed hours and closing days, Monday opening, and parking. Where Gunsan Culture and Tourism and Korea Tourism Organization give different values, we list both and add 'Call before visiting'.

body.heading: Gunsan City designates 34 places as 2026 Gunsan Matjip and 51 as Model Restaurants; 19 of the places on this page are designated
body.text: The Gunsan Culture and Tourism website posts the Gunsan Matjip designation table (34 places in 2026) and the Model Restaurant list (51 places) separately. Counting the 15 places on both lists once, the total is 70. Of the places on this page, 4 are on both lists: Ssangyong Banjeom, Gyegok Garden, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch and Saemangeum Hoetjip. 6 are designated Gunsan Matjip only: Bokseongnu, Ilpum Agu, Yujeong Chobap, Jin Galbi, Ilhaeok and Myeongdong Soba. 9 are designated Model Restaurants only: Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch, Arirang, Seou Sikdang, Jejudo Hoetjip, Eosijang Hwareohoe Jikgeorae Panmaejang, Gunsan Tteokgalbi, Welmiga Susong Branch, Singane Kalguksu and Janggane. The Daejeong Soba in the Gunsan Matjip table is at 36 Guyeong 7-gil, but the Daejeong Soba on this page is at 34-1 Guyeong 7-gil. Call before visiting to check whether they are the same business (063-445-4808). The 34 Gunsan Matjip places are covered in the guide on Gunsan City's designated restaurants, and the 51 model restaurants in the guide on Gunsan's model restaurants and good-price restaurants, each with menus, hours, parking and phones.

body.heading: Gunsan jjamppong is concentrated in the 9 restaurants of the Jjamppong Street on Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong; off the street, Ssangyong Banjeom, Bokseongnu, Jirinseong, Wangsan Banjeom and others serve it
body.text: Gunsan Culture and Tourism groups 9 places as the Jjamppong Street (Chinese food): Gaebok-dong Jungsikdang, Junghwa Jjamppong, Gunsan Ojingeo Jjamppong, Mingyu Jjamppong, Jumbo Jjamppong, Junghwa Banjeom 1968, Junghwa Banjeom, Hongyeongjang and Binhaewon. All have addresses on Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong. Of the 9, menus are listed for Hongyeongjang (jjamppong, mul-jjajang, tangsuyuk and more) and Binhaewon (Gunsan samseon jjamppong, gan-jjajang, yuni-jjajang and more). Add the 18 places off the street with jjamppong dishes, and jjamppong dishes are on the menu at 20 places (including Halbae Guksu's beef jjamppong ramen). Off the street, Ssangyong Banjeom in Geum-dong, labeled a 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data, serves jjamppong (clam jjamppong and abalone jjamppong). So do Bokseongnu (jjamppong and mul-jjajang) and Jirinseong (chili jjamppong) in Miwon-dong, Wangsan Banjeom in Munhwa-dong (bean sprout jjamppong and white jjamppong), and Susong Banjeom on Dongme 3-gil (seafood jjamppong and whole-squid seafood jjamppong). Of these, the ones open on Monday are Hongyeongjang (no regular closing day), Bokseongnu (closed Sundays and public holidays), Jirinseong and Wangsan Banjeom (closed every Tuesday) and Susong Banjeom (closed every Thursday). Binhaewon closes every Monday. Ssangyong Banjeom's closing days differ by source: open all year according to Gunsan City, but closed on the second and fourth Mondays of each month according to Korea Tourism Organization. Call before visiting. The guide 'Where and when to eat jjamppong, marinated blue crab and bakdae in Gunsan' lists how many places are open on each day of the week and their afternoon breaks.

body.heading: Kkotgejang (marinated blue crab) is a signature dish at 9 places in Gunsan, including Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch, Hanjuok and Gyegok Garden, and 6 of them are open all year
body.text: Kkotgejang is in the signature menu at 9 places, under the names kkotgejang, kkotgejang set meal, kkotgejang baekban (with rice and side dishes), Gungjeon kkotgejang set meal and myeongpum kkotgejang. They are Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch, Gyegok Garden, Yuseong Garden, Daido, Daega Kkotgejang, Cheongdam Hoetjip Main Branch, Hanjuok and Haedam. Add Jangguk Myeongga, Hansokkeum and Yurak Sikdang, which have gejang among their other menu items, and the total is 12. Of the 9, 6 are listed as open all year: Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch (11:00–20:00), Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch (10:00–21:30), Yuseong Garden (10:00–21:00), Cheongdam Hoetjip Main Branch (Monday–Saturday 12:00–22:30, Sunday 12:00–22:00), Hanjuok (11:00–21:00) and Gyegok Garden. Gyegok Garden's hours differ by source (11:00–21:30 according to Gunsan City, 11:00–20:30 according to Korea Tourism Organization), so call before visiting (063-453-0608). Daido closes every Sunday, Daega Kkotgejang every Monday and Haedam every Tuesday. Parking is free at Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch. Gyegok Garden has room for 100 cars and Yuseong Garden for 50. Hanjuok has no parking.

body.heading: In Gunsan, bakdae is on the menu at Saemangeum Hoetjip, Arirang and Namdo Bapsang; jogitang (yellow croaker stew) is the signature dish at Yurak Sikdang, and mulmegi stew at Ilpung Sikdang
body.text: Bakdae dishes are on the menu at 3 places. Saemangeum Hoetjip in Bieungdo-dong lists bakdae stew according to Gunsan City and a bakdae set meal according to Korea Tourism Organization. Arirang in Jangmi-dong serves a golden bakdae set meal, and Namdo Bapsang on Seonyubuk-gil in Okdo-myeon serves a Gunsan grilled bakdae set meal. Namdo Bapsang is open all year, 09:00–19:30 on weekdays and 08:30–20:00 on weekends. Saemangeum Hoetjip is also open all year according to both sources. Arirang's closing days differ by source (the second and fourth Mondays according to Gunsan City, the first and third Mondays according to Korea Tourism Organization), so call before visiting (063-442-1207, or 0507-1383-1207 on the Gunsan City sanitation list). Places with fish stew as a signature dish include Yurak Sikdang on Haemang-ro, labeled a 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data. It serves jogitang (yellow croaker stew), plus anagotang (conger eel stew) and seodae stew, and closes every Monday. Ilpung Sikdang on Seoheung 1-gil serves mulmegi stew and geonmegi stew (07:00–21:00, closed every Monday). Huirak (fish stew) and Gyeongwon Anago (conger eel stew), classified as soup and stew restaurants, are also options.

body.heading: Monkfish (agwi or agu) dishes in Gunsan: signature dishes at Seou Sikdang (agwi baekban), Ilpum Agu (agutang) and Jejudo Hoetjip (agujjim), and on the menu at 6 more, including Gugil Sikdang and Gyeongwon Haemuljjim
body.text: Monkfish dishes appear under the names agujjim (braised monkfish), agutang (monkfish stew), agwijjim and agwi baekban at 9 places. They are Seou Sikdang, Jejudo Hoetjip, Haesong, Gunsan Bokjip, Ilpum Agu, Yurak Sikdang, Gugil Sikdang, Gyeongwon Haemuljjim and Ilpum Hoejip. As a signature dish, Seou Sikdang serves agwi baekban (monkfish with rice and side dishes); it closes every Sunday and has no parking. Ilpum Agu in Susong-dong serves agutang (10:00–22:00, closed on the first and third Sundays). Jejudo Hoetjip in Susong-dong serves agujjim along with sliced raw fish and fish stew. Gugil Sikdang in Jukseong-dong, labeled a 'Good Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data, has bokjjim (braised pufferfish) as its signature dish and also serves agujjim (closed every Monday). Gyeongwon Haemuljjim serves agwijjim and gonijjim (braised fish roe) along with haemuljjim (braised seafood), and closes every Sunday. Ilpum Hoejip in Mijang-dong is open all year, 11:30–22:00, and serves agujjim, fresh rockfish stew and mulhoe (raw fish soup).

body.heading: Raw fish (hoe) and sushi in Gunsan are signature dishes at raw fish restaurants such as Eosijang Hwareohoe Jikgeorae Panmaejang, Gunsan Daejeon Hoetjip and Hyeondae Hoetjip, and at the sushi restaurants Yujeong Chobap and Dombe Chobap
body.text: Raw fish (saengseonhoe or hwareohoe), a raw fish set meal, sashimi or sushi is in the signature menu at 11 places. They are Wando Hoejip, Eosijang Hwareohoe Jikgeorae Panmaejang, Deungdaero, Bada Hoejip Hyeondae Core Branch, Yujeong Chobap, Jejudo Hoetjip, Haesong, Gunsan Daejeon Hoetjip, Gunsan Ilsik, Dombe Chobap and Hyeondae Hoetjip. Deungdaero's signature menu differs by source: a raw fish course (hwareohoe) according to Korea Tourism Organization, but fresh clam and mushroom hot pot and spicy rockfish stew according to Gunsan City. Call before visiting (0507-1442-9500). Wando Hoejip and Deungdaero are in Bieungdo-dong, Eosijang Hwareohoe Jikgeorae Panmaejang and Jejudo Hoetjip in Susong-dong, and Bada Hoejip Hyeondae Core Branch and Haesong in Naun-dong. Eosijang Hwareohoe Jikgeorae Panmaejang opens 10:00–23:00 and closes only on the day of traditional holidays. Gunsan Daejeon Hoetjip and Hyeondae Hoetjip close every Monday, and Gunsan Ilsik every Sunday. Sushi is the signature dish at Yujeong Chobap in Yeonghwa-dong (closed on the first and third Mondays) and Dombe Chobap on Susongnam-ro (closed every Tuesday). Mulgogijari in Bieungdo-dong has the Tangjeoksik Special as its signature dish and also serves raw fish set meals, mulhoe and hoedeopbap (raw fish over rice). It is open all year, 11:00–22:00, and parking is free.

body.heading: Tteokgalbi is a signature dish at Gunsan Tteokgalbi, Jin Galbi, Wanjuok and others; at Gunsan Tteokgalbi in Mijang-dong, hanu (Korean beef) tteokgalbi (200 g) costs 24,000 won
body.text: Tteokgalbi is in the signature menu at 6 places: Gunsan Tteokgalbi, Wanjuok, Jin Galbi, Nae Galbi, Hanu Tteokgalbi and Mosanbang. Mosanbang's signature menu differs by source: a tteokgalbi set meal according to Korea Tourism Organization, but fusion hanjeongsik (Korean set meal) according to Gunsan City. Call before visiting (063-463-4411, or 0507-1468-4412 on the Gunsan City sanitation list). Gunsan Tteokgalbi lists prices of 24,000 won for hanu (Korean beef) tteokgalbi (200 g) and 11,000 won for pork tteokgalbi (200 g). It closes every Tuesday. Jin Galbi (Yeonghwa-dong, closed every Monday), Wanjuok, Nae Galbi and Hanu Tteokgalbi also serve gomtang. Wanjuok's closing days differ by source: open all year according to Gunsan City, but closed every Wednesday according to Korea Tourism Organization. Call before visiting (063-445-2644). For grilled galbi (ribs), Myeongwol Galbi in Sinchang-dong (seasoned beef ribs, open all year) and Wonpung Galbi on Jinpo-ro (fresh ribs, closed on Seollal and Chuseok days) serve it as a signature dish. Both have free parking. Of the places on this site, Gunsan Culture and Tourism classifies 12 as meat (charcoal grill). One of them is Gunsan Hanuchon in Singwan-dong (fresh sirloin and galbitang, 10:00–22:00, open all year except traditional holidays).

body.heading: Kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) in Gunsan: Welmiga Susong Branch serves it 24 hours, Ilhaeok from 04:00 and Ilheungok from 05:00
body.text: Kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) is served at 4 places: Welmiga Susong Branch, Hyeondaeok (Mijang Branch), Ilhaeok and Ilheungok. Welmiga Susong Branch in Susong-dong serves kongnamul gukbap and spicy pork rice soup 24 hours a day, all year. Ilhaeok on Guyeong 7-gil in Wolmyeong-dong is open all year, 04:00–15:00. Ilheungok on the same street opens 05:00–15:00 and closes every Wednesday. Mijuok on Guyeong 7-gil, labeled a 'Good Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data, serves dakgomtang (chicken soup) 06:00–14:00. Hanirok on Guyeong 3-gil serves hanu muguk (Korean beef and radish soup) 07:00–21:30 and is open all year. Jeonju Ujok Seolleongtang in Geumgwang-dong serves ujoktang (ox trotter soup), seolleongtang and galbitang (rib soup) 06:00–20:30 and closes on traditional holidays. Unjeong Sikdang, labeled a 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data, serves mung bean samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), ujoktang and seolleongtang 11:00–20:00. It closes every Monday.

body.heading: Kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) is a signature dish at Singane Kalguksu, Janggane and Jangmi Kalguksu, and soba at Daejeong Soba, Myeongdong Soba, Seosomun Soba and others
body.text: Kalguksu is served at 6 places. They are Geumgang Haemul Kalguksu (abalone kalguksu) and Singane Kalguksu in Seongsan-myeon, Janggane in Bieungdo-dong, Namdo Bapsang (Seonyudo Manila clam kalguksu) and Seonyudo Bambada (seafood kalguksu) in Okdo-myeon, and Jangmi Kalguksu on Keunsaem-gil. Singane Kalguksu serves pat kalguksu (red bean kalguksu), bajirak kalguksu (Manila clam kalguksu) and saenghap kalguksu, and has a children's playroom. Janggane also serves Manila clam dishes such as Manila clam porridge and seasoned raw Manila clams, and closes every Tuesday. Jangmi Kalguksu opens only 10:00–16:00 and closes every Wednesday. Soba is the signature dish at 4 places. Daejeong Soba in Wolmyeong-dong is open all year, 10:00–20:00. Myeongdong Soba in Jangmi-dong serves mori soba and deulgireum bibim memil (buckwheat noodles mixed with perilla oil), and closes on Sundays in winter. Seosomun Soba in Naun-dong serves cold soba 11:00–15:10 and closes every Monday. Seoul Soba closes every Sunday.

body.heading: Gunsan bakeries with bread as the signature item include Iseongdang (sweet red bean bun), Yeongguk Ppangjip (white glutinous barley sweet red bean bun), Ppang Gumneun Onammae (white glutinous barley butse) and Hongyun Bakery (jjamppong bread)
body.text: Bread or hotteok is the signature item at 7 places. They are Iseongdang (danpatppang, a sweet red bean bun), Yeongguk Ppangjip (white glutinous barley sweet red bean bun), Ppang Gumneun Onammae (white glutinous barley butse) and Hongyun Bakery (jjamppong bread). The others are Mulmilso (Korean-wheat sourdough), TEUM (croissant ang-butter, with red bean paste and butter) and Gunsan Jungdong Hotteok (Jungdong hotteok). Sweet red bean buns are on the menu at 3 places: Iseongdang, Yeongguk Ppangjip and Ppang Gumneun Onammae. Bread made with white glutinous barley is at Yeongguk Ppangjip and Ppang Gumneun Onammae. In the morning, Ppang Gumneun Onammae opens at 07:30, and Iseongdang and Yeongguk Ppangjip at 08:00. Iseongdang and Yeongguk Ppangjip have no parking. Iseongdang has irregular closing days, so call before visiting. Iseongdang is a stop on Gunsan City's travel Course 2 (Tangnyu Course). Mulmilso closes every Sunday and Monday, and closes early when the bread runs out.

body.heading: The Gunsan restaurants that appear in broadcaster channel YouTube videos linked on this site are 6: Iseongdang, Mannam Snack, Hanjuok, Gunsan Jungdong Hotteok, Bihaengjang Jeongmun Budaejjigae and Yeongguk Ppangjip
body.text: Of the YouTube videos collected on this site, 7 from broadcaster channels cover Gunsan restaurants. Iseongdang and Mannam Snack appear in 2 each, and Yeongguk Ppangjip and Bihaengjang Jeongmun Budaejjigae in 1 each. Hanjuok and Gunsan Jungdong Hotteok appear together in 1 video. Mannam Snack on Daehak-ro serves japtang, kimchi fried rice, stir-fried sundae (Korean sausage) and gimbap 11:00–19:30. Bihaengjang Jeongmun Budaejjigae on Hanaunan 2-gil serves budaejjigae (army stew) and hamburgers 10:00–21:00. Both close every Monday. Gunsan Jungdong Hotteok on Seorae-ro sells Jungdong hotteok and mulberry leaf cream cheese hotteok and is open all year. You can watch the videos on each restaurant's page.

body.heading: Of the Gunsan restaurants on this site, 3 are labeled 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data: Ssangyong Banjeom, Unjeong Sikdang and Yurak Sikdang
body.text: Among the restaurants on this site, 3 have 'Baengnyeon Gage' (Hundred-Year Shop) before their business name in Korea Tourism Organization data. They are Ssangyong Banjeom in Geum-dong (clam jjamppong), Unjeong Sikdang on Jungjeong-gil (mung bean samgyetang) and Yurak Sikdang on Haemang-ro (jogitang). Unjeong Sikdang and Yurak Sikdang close every Monday. The 'Chakan Gage' (Good Shop) label appears before the name of 5 places. They are Gayajang (jjamppong, closed every Monday) and Aseowon (gan-jjajang, closed every Thursday) in Gyeongam-dong, and Gugil Sikdang in Jukseong-dong (bokjjim and agujjim). The others are Mijuok in Yeonghwa-dong (dakgomtang) and Seonhyeon Daesot Ttukkeong Galbi in Naun-dong (samgyeopsal, or pork belly; open all year).

items.reason: This Chinese restaurant at 121 Naehang 2-gil in Geum-dong is labeled a 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data. Its signature dish is jogae jjamppong (clam jjamppong), and it also serves abalone jjamppong, jjajangmyeon, tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) and more. Hours and closing days differ by source. Gunsan City lists 11:30–21:00, open all year. Korea Tourism Organization lists 11:30–19:00, closing early when ingredients run out, and closed on the second and fourth Mondays of each month. Call before visiting (063-445-2633, or 063-443-1259 on the Gunsan City sanitation list). It has parking for 7 cars and 40 seats. Gunsan City has designated it both a 2026 Gunsan Matjip and a Model Restaurant.

This Chinese restaurant at 57 Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong, on the Jjamppong Street, has jjajangmyeon as its signature dish. It also serves Gunsan samseon jjamppong, gan-jjajang, yuni-jjajang and more. Both sources list it as closed every Monday, and parking is free. Hours differ between Gunsan City (10:00–21:00) and Korea Tourism Organization (weekdays 10:30–20:00, weekends 10:00–20:00), so call before visiting (063-445-2429).

This Chinese restaurant at 42 Dongnyeong-gil on the Jjamppong Street has jjajangmyeon as its signature dish and also serves jjamppong, mul-jjajang, tangsuyuk and more. It opens 11:00–15:00 on weekdays and 11:00–18:00 on weekends. It has no regular closing day, so it is open on Monday. It has 50 seats and parking.

This Chinese restaurant at 382 Wolmyeong-ro in Miwon-dong serves jjamppong, jjamppong-bap (jjamppong with rice), mul-jjajang, fried rice and more. Its signature dish is seafood jjamppong according to Gunsan City but jjajangmyeon according to Korea Tourism Organization, so call before visiting (063-445-8412). It opens only 10:00–16:00 and closes on Sundays and public holidays, so it is open on Monday. It has 35 seats, uses a public parking lot and takes phone reservations. It is a 2026 Gunsan Matjip designated by Gunsan City.

This restaurant at 87 Miwon-ro in Miwon-dong has chili jjajang as its signature dish and also serves chili jjamppong, jjamppong, chili jjamppong-bap and more. It opens 10:00–15:00 on weekdays and 09:30–16:00 on weekends but closes early when ingredients run out. It closes every Tuesday, so it is open on Monday. Parking and takeout are available.

This restaurant at 209 Daehak-ro in Munhwa-dong has kongnamul jjamppong (bean sprout jjamppong) as its signature dish. It also serves spicy jjamppong, baek-jjamppong (white jjamppong), jjajangmyeon, jjamppong-bap and more. It opens 10:00–18:00 and closes every Tuesday. Parking is available, but takeout is not.

This restaurant at 31 Guyeong 2-gil has the kkotgejang (marinated blue crab) set meal as its signature dish. It also serves kkotgejang baekban (with rice and side dishes), and daehajang (marinated king prawn) as a set meal or baekban. It is open all year, 11:00–21:00, and offers takeout and phone reservations (063-443-3812). There is no parking. It appears in 1 broadcaster channel video.

This restaurant on Gungpo 1-ro in Jochon-dong has the Gungjeon kkotgejang (marinated blue crab) set meal as its signature dish. It also serves a kkotgejang set meal, a blue crab stew set meal, seasoned blue crab, steamed blue crab and more. It is open all year, 10:00–21:30, with 240 seats and free parking. Gunsan City has designated it both a 2026 Gunsan Matjip and a Model Restaurant.

This restaurant at 470 Geumgang-ro in Gaejeong-myeon has kkotgejang baekban (marinated blue crab with rice and side dishes) as its signature dish according to Gunsan City, and ganjang gejang (soy-marinated crab) according to Korea Tourism Organization. It also serves yangnyeom gejang (seasoned marinated crab), jeonbokjang (marinated abalone), blue crab stew and more. Both sources list it as open all year, but hours differ: 11:00–21:30 according to Gunsan City and 11:00–20:30 according to Korea Tourism Organization. Call before visiting (063-453-0608). It has parking for 100 cars and 400 seats. Gunsan City has designated it both a 2026 Gunsan Matjip and a Model Restaurant.

This restaurant at 70 Guyeong 3-gil in Sinchang-dong has kkotgejang (marinated blue crab) and assorted soy-marinated seafood as its signature dishes. Its kkotgejang is aged in soy sauce for 72 hours. It is open all year, 11:00–20:00, and has 40 seats. It is a Model Restaurant designated by Gunsan City.

This raw fish restaurant at 13 Bieungan 7-gil in Bieungdo-dong lists bakdae as bakdae stew according to Gunsan City and as a bakdae set meal according to Korea Tourism Organization. It also serves a fresh clam (saenghap) set meal, a raw fish set meal, course meals and more. Both sources list it as open all year, but hours differ: 10:00–22:00 according to Gunsan City, and 11:00–22:00 with a break 15:00–17:00 according to Korea Tourism Organization. Call before visiting (063-464-1001). It has parking for 50 cars and 180 seats. Gunsan City has designated it both a 2026 Gunsan Matjip and a Model Restaurant.

This Korean restaurant at 224 Haemang-ro in Jangmi-dong has the golden bakdae set meal and white glutinous barley bibimbap as its signature dishes. It also serves barley pork cutlet, barley hoedeopbap (raw fish over rice) and more. Closing days differ by source: the second and fourth Mondays according to Gunsan City, and the first and third Mondays according to Korea Tourism Organization. Call before visiting (063-442-1207, or 0507-1383-1207 on the Gunsan City sanitation list). It has parking for 100 cars and 120 seats, and offers takeout. It is a Model Restaurant designated by Gunsan City.

This restaurant at 79 Seonyubuk-gil in Okdo-myeon has the Gunsan grilled bakdae set meal as its signature dish. It also serves cockle bibimbap, Seonyudo Manila clam kalguksu, handmade pork cutlet and more. It is open all year, 09:00–19:30 on weekdays and 08:30–20:00 on weekends, with parking and takeout.

faq.q: Where are good places to eat in Gunsan?
faq.a: By dish: for jjamppong, go to the 9 restaurants on the Jjamppong Street on Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong, or to Ssangyong Banjeom, Bokseongnu and Jirinseong. For kkotgejang (marinated blue crab), go to Hanjuok, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch and Gyegok Garden. For bakdae, go to Saemangeum Hoetjip, Arirang and Namdo Bapsang, and for tteokgalbi, Gunsan Tteokgalbi and Jin Galbi. For kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup), go to Ilhaeok, Ilheungok and Welmiga Susong Branch, and for bread, Iseongdang and Yeongguk Ppangjip. Of the 172 Gunsan restaurants on this site, 20 have jjamppong dishes on the menu, 12 have gejang (marinated crab) and 9 have agwi or agu (monkfish).

faq.q: Where can I eat jjamppong in Gunsan?
faq.a: The Jjamppong Street on Dongnyeong-gil in Jangmi-dong has 9 Chinese restaurants: Gaebok-dong Jungsikdang, Junghwa Jjamppong, Gunsan Ojingeo Jjamppong, Mingyu Jjamppong, Jumbo Jjamppong, Junghwa Banjeom 1968, Junghwa Banjeom, Hongyeongjang and Binhaewon. Off the street, Ssangyong Banjeom in Geum-dong (clam jjamppong), labeled a 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data, serves jjamppong. So do Bokseongnu (10:00–16:00, closed Sundays and public holidays) and Jirinseong (chili jjamppong, closed every Tuesday) in Miwon-dong, and Wangsan Banjeom in Munhwa-dong (bean sprout jjamppong). Of the restaurants on this site, 20 have jjamppong dishes on the menu, including Hongyeongjang and Binhaewon on the street.

faq.q: Where can I eat kkotgejang (marinated blue crab) in Gunsan?
faq.a: Among the restaurants on this site, 9 have kkotgejang in their signature menu. They are Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch, Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch, Gyegok Garden, Yuseong Garden, Daido, Daega Kkotgejang, Cheongdam Hoetjip Main Branch, Hanjuok and Haedam. Of these, 6 are open all year: Jjaebo Sikdang Main Branch (11:00–20:00), Gungjeon Kkotgejang Main Branch (10:00–21:30, free parking), Yuseong Garden (10:00–21:00), Cheongdam Hoetjip Main Branch, Hanjuok (11:00–21:00, no parking) and Gyegok Garden.

faq.q: Are there bakeries in Gunsan other than Iseongdang?
faq.a: Yes. Yeongguk Ppangjip (white glutinous barley sweet red bean bun, 08:00–21:00, closed on Seollal) has bread as its signature item. So do Ppang Gumneun Onammae (white glutinous barley butse, 07:30–22:00, closed every Sunday) and Hongyun Bakery (jjamppong bread, closed on the third and fifth Wednesdays of each month). Mulmilso (Korean-wheat sourdough) and TEUM (croissant ang-butter) do too. Iseongdang's signature item is the sweet red bean bun, and it opens 08:00–21:30 Sunday–Thursday and 08:00–22:00 on Friday and Saturday.

faq.q: Which Gunsan restaurants have appeared in broadcasts?
faq.a: In broadcaster channel YouTube videos linked on this site, 6 Gunsan restaurants appear. They are Iseongdang and Mannam Snack (2 videos each), Hanjuok and Gunsan Jungdong Hotteok (together in 1 video), and Bihaengjang Jeongmun Budaejjigae and Yeongguk Ppangjip (1 video each). Mannam Snack's signature dish is japtang, and Bihaengjang Jeongmun Budaejjigae's is budaejjigae (army stew). Both close every Monday.

Of the Gunsan restaurants on this site, 3 are labeled 'Hundred-Year Shop' in Korea Tourism Organization data. They are Ssangyong Banjeom (Naehang 2-gil, Geum-dong; clam jjamppong), Unjeong Sikdang (Jungjeong-gil; mung bean samgyetang) and Yurak Sikdang (Haemang-ro; jogitang, or yellow croaker stew). Unjeong Sikdang and Yurak Sikdang close every Monday. Ssangyong Banjeom's closing days differ by source (open all year according to Gunsan City, the second and fourth Mondays of each month according to Korea Tourism Organization), so call before visiting (063-445-2633, or 063-443-1259 on the Gunsan City sanitation list).
